title: Localization framework + first translated lessons
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). Once the curriculum is proven with English content, localizing it into other languages dramatically expands the beneficiary pool. The schema must anticipate i18n without requiring it in early phases; this task adds the localization framework (code) and produces the first set of translated lessons (writing/translation), gated on an i18n schema decision.
objective: Add a localization framework to the schema and tooling (supporting multiple UI language translations of lesson content) and produce the first translated set of lessons in at least one non-English language, demonstrating the i18n model end-to-end.
acceptanceCriteria: An i18n schema decision is recorded before authoring begins: how language variants are modeled in the lesson schema (e.g. a locale field, a translations map, or parallel files).
The localization framework is implemented: the schema supports at least one non-English locale, the site renders locale-selected content, and the tooling validates translated content.
At least 3 lessons from the Python module are translated into a non-English language by a qualified human translator; no machine-only translations without human review.
Translated lessons are schema-valid and carry translator attribution and a locale tag.
Technical accuracy of translated content is reviewed by a reviewer fluent in the target language.
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass.
output: A merged PR adding the localization framework and at least 3 translated lessons in a non-English language, with translator attribution and schema-valid locale metadata.
